title: 'Three Banks Lose Buy Ratings as Bond Yields Rise; Hong Leong Names PBBANK Its 4Q Top Pick
text:
'Three Banks Lose Buy Ratings as Bond Yields Rise; Hong Leong Names PBBANK Its 4Q Top Pick

'Hong Leong Investment Bank analyst Raymond Ng Ing Yeow downgraded AMMB Holdings, CIMB Group Holdings and RHB Bank to “Hold” from “Buy” in a banking-sector review. He cut their target prices to RM6.70 from RM7.80, RM8.10 from RM8.70 and RM8.00 from RM9.50, respectively. In contrast, he upgraded Public Bank to “Buy” from “Hold” and raised its target price to RM5.30 from RM4.90, naming it his top banking pick for 4Q26. Raymond Ng Ing Yeow is ranked No.10 among 17 financial services analysts on StockTipRatings, based on data since 2023. He holds a 66% expert rating, with a 7% average return and a 56% success rate across stocks he covered over the one-year period following his calls. The changes come as the yield on 10-year Malaysian Government Securities rose to 3.94% on September 25 from 3.60% at end-June. Higher yields reduce the market value of bonds already held by banks, potentially weighing on treasury-related non-interest income before the benefit of reinvesting at higher yields emerges. Raymond said the immediate impact appears manageable, but repeated increases in yields could make earnings less predictable and limit further gains in bank valuations. Under his hypothetical 30-basis-point yield-rise scenario, the estimated gross mark-to-market impact for AMMB Holdings and Bank Islam Malaysia is equivalent to about 10% of their projected annual non-interest income, compared with 4.5% for CIMB Group Holdings and 3.2% for RHB Bank. Public Bank’s direct earnings sensitivity is lower at 1.3%. These are pre-tax estimates that exclude hedging and other offsets—not cuts to earnings forecasts. Raymond said the three downgrades reflect weaker visibility over non-interest income and a higher hurdle for bank-share valuations to rise further. He favours Public Bank for its exceptionally low impaired-loan ratio, resilient earnings and relatively limited direct earnings exposure to the bond-market sell-off, although its bond holdings could still affect book value. He maintained a “Neutral” sector view, noting that foreign investors sold a net RM1.3 billion of Malaysian banking shares between July 1 and September 25, while higher bond yields have made fixed-income investments more competitive. As of 2:09 p.m. on September 29, the Bursa Malaysia Financial Services index dropped 1% to 19,394.6 points. title: 'Benign inflation keeps OPR outlook intact: CIMB Securities
text:
'Benign inflation keeps OPR outlook intact: CIMB Securities

'KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's inflation may remain benign despite firmer monthly price increases and rising food and electricity costs, according to CIMB Securities.   The research house said headline inflation rose to 1.9 per cent year-on-year (YoY) in August from 1.8 per cent in July, while core inflation eased to 1.7 per cent from 1.8 per cent, largely due to favourable base effects in information and communication.   However, both headline and core prices rose 0.3 per cent month-on-month (MoM), compared with no change in July, indicating firmer sequential price momentum.

title: 'Mateen perlu RM8,000 beli ‘stroller’ khas
text:
'Mateen perlu RM8,000 beli ‘stroller’ khas

'PETALING JAYA – Bayi hidrosefalus, Muhammad Mateen Aryan Muhammad Hanif, 15 bulan, dari Sungai Petani, Kedah, kini semakin aktif namun pergerakannya terbatas disebabkan kepalanya yang berat. Bapanya, Muhammad Hanif Zakaria, 32, berkata, Mateen kini cuba menggerakkan badan dan memusingkan badan, tetapi sukar berbuat demikian dengan kepala yang mencecah ukuran 90 sentimeter (cm). “Perkembangan dia okey. Dia pun cuba bergerak, nak pusing badannya, tetapi tak boleh sebab kepala dia berat,” katanya ketika dihubungi Kosmo!. Menurut Muhammad Hanif, keadaan Mateen kini semakin baik apabila sawan yang dialaminya semakin berkurang, namun apabila serangan berlaku, saiz kepala anaknya boleh kembali membesar. “Sejak kami mendapatkan rawatan alternatif, Mateen semakin kurang diserang sawan dan saiz kepala dia turun sedikit ke 89cm. Tapi apabila kena sawan, automatik saiz tu boleh naik balik,” ujarnya. Muhammad Hanif berkata, keperluan asas Matten kini mencukupi dan berterima kasih kepada pihak yang pernah membantu, namun dia dan isteri kini merancang untuk mendapatkan kereta sorong (stroller) khas bagi memudahkan pergerakan Mateen. Bagaimanapun dia menjelaskan, ia perlu ditempah khas mengikut keperluan Mateen, dengan anggaran kos sebanyak RM8,000 dan akan berbuat demikian apabila jumlah itu mencukupi. Orang ramai yang ingin membantu keluarga itu mendapatkan kereta sorong berkenaan, boleh menyalurkan sumbangan ke akaun bank CIMB bernombor 7632966954 di atas nama Muhammad Hanif. Terdahulu Kosmo! melaporkan, Muhammad Hanif yang bekerja sebagai pemandu lori bersyukur kerana anak bongsu daripada tiga beradik itu tidak pernah menangis kesakitan sejak lahir. Dia dan isteri, Habidah Nasruddin, 31, bagaimanapun berdepan kesukaran mengangkat Mateen disebabkan kepalanya yang makin membesar. title: 'RHB Bank sees more upside for 4Q26
text:
'RHB Bank sees more upside for 4Q26

'PETALING JAYA: RHB Bank Bhd’s management has shared that there is sufficient runway to reposition the bank’s portfolio and capitalise on market opportunities for the fourth quarter ending Dec 31, 2026 (4Q26) after surging Malaysian Government Securities (MGS) yields weigh on non- interest income (NOII) in 3Q26. Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) Research said the bank’s near-term outlook faces pressure from elevated MGS yields, which could weigh on its 3Q26 NOII, but that management appears less downbeat on the 4Q26 outlook should MGS yields stabilise or retrace. The research house, which recently met with the bank’s management, maintained a “hold” call and target price of RM8 based on implied one time 2027 price to book, as most near-term drivers have been baked in, with no stronger immediate catalyst. “We came away from a recent meeting with RHB’s management feeling neutral on its earnings trajectory and asset quality outlook,” it said, with weaker trading income largely inevitable given the limited runway for recovery during 3Q26. “While stronger wealth, bancassurance/takaful, investment banking, brokerage and loan-related fees should provide some cushion, these are unlikely to fully offset the trading-income shortfall.” The research firm said the impact on 3Q26 should be viewed more as a foregone trading upside rather than outsized losses, given RHB’s relatively small trading book. The Treasury has been tactically unwinding securities positions, crystallising gains where possible while reducing exposure. The bank’s return on equity (ROE) target range of 10.8% to 11% appears within reach despite the NOII headwinds, but only towards the lower end as the burden increasingly shifts to core operations, with loan growth of 6% and management having reset cost growth to less than or equal to 1%, providing scope for better operating leverage. “Credit cost is tracking around the lower end of its 13 basis points (bps) to 14bps guidance, with management comfortable at 13bps and hopeful of achieving 12bps should recoveries materialise,” HLIB Research said. Wealth sales have also risen 35% year-on-year as of June 2026, while bancassurance/takaful, brokerage and loan-related fees continue to gain traction. Taken together, these levers should partially cushion the NOII drag, although the path towards the upper end of management’s ROE ambition has become more challenging amid elevated bond yields. Capital management remains an important medium-term catalyst, with management targeting more clarity on its capital/dividend policy by 1Q27. The priority would be to ensure operations and targeted growth trajectory can be adequately funded while sustaining Common Equity Tier 1 around current levels. Should these growth requirements be met without absorbing the existing surplus, the excess capital could potentially be fully returned to shareholders. The existing dividend remains respectable, with projected dividend yield of 6.

title: 'F1 Bukan Anjuran MOTAC, Tapi Peluang Besar Promosikan Malaysia
text:
'F1 Bukan Anjuran MOTAC, Tapi Peluang Besar Promosikan Malaysia

'Intipati berita - 300,000 pengunjung disasarkan hadir ke SIC, termasuk 50,000 pelancong antarabangsa. - F1 dijangka menjana impak ekonomi sekitar RM1.3 bilion kepada Malaysia. - MOTAC & Tourism Malaysia menyediakan pakej pelancongan untuk menggalakkan pelancong asing tinggal lebih lama di Malaysia. - F1 turut menjadi platform mempromosikan pelancongan, budaya dan seni Malaysia sempena Kempen Melawat Malaysia 2026–2027. Kementerian Pelancongan, Seni dan Budaya (MOTAC) menyasarkan kehadiran kira-kira 300,000 pengunjung sempena penganjuran Formula One (F1) Grand Prix (GP) Bahrain di Litar Antarabangsa Sepang (SIC) dari 2 hingga 4 Oktober. Menurut laporan Berita RTM, daripada jumlah itu, kira-kira 50,000 pelancong antarabangsa dijangka hadir ke SIC bagi menyaksikan perlumbaan berprestij tersebut. Ketua Komunikasi Korporat MOTAC, Firna Azura Ekaputri Marzuki berkata, berdasarkan unjuran Hong Leong Bank Research, penganjuran F1 itu dijangka memberi impak ekonomi sekitar RM1.3 bilion. Berdasarkan data penyelidikan Hong Leong Bank, penganjuran F1 ini sahaja dijangka mampu menjana pendapatan sebanyak RM1.3 bilion melalui sektor pelancongan sukan dan perbelanjaan pelancong asing. Setakat ini, kita menyasarkan kehadiran kira-kira 50,000 pelancong antarabangsa daripada keseluruhan 300,000 pengunjung yang dijangka membanjiri SIC bagi menyaksikan Grand Prix F1 tersebut. MOTAC ada sediakan pakej pelancongan? Menurut Firna Azura, penganjuran F1 ini turut bertepatan dengan Kempen Melawat Malaysia 2026–2027 dan menjadi platform untuk memperkenalkan budaya, seni serta produk pelancongan negara kepada pelancong antarabangsa. MOTAC menerusi Tourism Malaysia bersama SIC turut menyediakan beberapa pakej pelancongan bagi menggalakkan pengunjung luar negara melanjutkan tempoh penginapan mereka di Malaysia. Selain menyaksikan F1, kita turut menggalakkan mereka untuk berbelanja, membeli-belah dan melakukan aktiviti pelancongan seperti melawat destinasi menarik di negara ini. Ini kerana selepas penganjuran F1 di Malaysia, saingan seterusnya akan berlangsung di Singapura. Siapa terlibat dalam persiapan penganjuran? Dalam pada itu, persiapan di bawah Jawatankuasa Publisiti, Promosi dan Pelancongan kini dilaporkan mencapai kira-kira 90 peratus. Pelbagai kementerian dan agensi terlibat bagi memastikan penganjuran berjalan lancar, antaranya KUSKOP, KBS, Kementerian Komunikasi, Tourism Malaysia, Kraftangan Malaysia, Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG), Majlis Perbandaran Sepang serta SIC. Apa maksudnya untuk anda? Bagi memeriahkan lagi penganjuran F1 hari kejadian, beberapa program berskala besar turut diatur dari 23 September hingga 4 Oktober. Antaranya ialah Litar Rasa MADANI, Sepang Food Festival di Mitsui Outlet Park, Citrawarna Speed Festival dan RIUH Pitstop di TRX. Selain itu, Malaysia International Craft Fair 2026 turut berlangsung di Kompleks Kraf Kuala Lumpur.

title: 'PTT Synergy beli 4 kilang dalam pembinaan bernilai RM32 juta di Klang jana hasil sewa berulang
text:
'PTT Synergy beli 4 kilang dalam pembinaan bernilai RM32 juta di Klang jana hasil sewa berulang

'KUALA LUMPUR 5 Okt — PTT Synergy Group Berhad bakal memperluas portfolio hartanah dengan pemerolehan empat unit kilang bernilai hampir RM32 juta di Klang, Selangor, yang disasarkan menjana pendapatan sewa berulang daripada penyewa industri. Menerusi makluman tambahan kepada Bursa Malaysia, ia berkata anak syarikat tidak langsung milik penuhnya, PTT Assets Sdn Bhd, akan memperoleh empat bidang tanah bersama unit kilang yang sedang atau akan dibina dengan jumlah pertimbangan tunai RM31.997 juta. Menurut kumpulan tersebut, pemerolehan itu bertujuan mengembangkan portfolio pelaburan hartanah kumpulan dan mewujudkan aliran pendapatan sewa berulang menerusi penyewaan keempat-empat unit kilang kepada penyewa industri. "PTT merancang memulakan proses mencari penyewa serta rundingan pajakan sepanjang tempoh pembinaan, dengan operasi sewaan disasarkan bermula selepas projek siap dan milikan kosong diserahkan, tertakluk kepada kerja pengubahsuaian yang diperlukan," katanya. Keempat-empat hartanah dijangka disiapkan dalam tempoh 36 bulan daripada tarikh perjanjian jual beli (SPA) masing-masing, dengan kerja pembinaan telah bermula pada 7 Januari 2026 dan kini mencapai sehingga peringkat rangka struktur bangunan, atau kira-kira 55% siap. Dari segi pembiayaan, risiko pembelian itu disokong kelulusan pinjaman daripada CIMB Bank Berhad dengan margin pembiayaan 90%, selain rebat Bumiputera 10% yang diberikan penjual. Berdasarkan terma pembayaran, 10% daripada harga pembelian perlu dibayar sebaik sahaja setiap SPA ditandatangani, manakala baki bayaran dibuat secara berperingkat mengikut kemajuan pembinaan sehingga notis milikan kosong dikeluarkan. "Pembelian itu turut mengambil kira transaksi hartanah perindustrian berdekatan, termasuk sebuah kilang berkembar di Bukit Raja Prime Industrial Park seluas 1,854.99 meter persegi yang didagangkan pada RM8.5 juta pada Jun 2026," jelas PTT. Satu lagi perbandingan ialah kilang berkembar di Bukit Raja 3 Industrial Park berkeluasan 2,024.99 meter persegi yang direkodkan pada harga RM7.689 juta pada Mac 2026. Sekiranya penjual gagal menyerahkan milikan kosong dalam tempoh 36 bulan daripada tarikh SPA, penjual perlu membayar ganti rugi dipersetujui pada kadar 5% setahun berdasarkan jumlah bayaran yang telah dibuat PTT sehingga tarikh penyerahan sebenar. Dari segi kedudukan kewangan, nisbah penggearan proforma PTT dijangka meningkat kepada 2.01 kali selepas pemerolehan berbanding 1.91 kali setakat 30 Jun 2025, berdasarkan kedudukan kewangan proforma yang dinyatakan syarikat. - DagangNews.com

title: 'Bursa Sheds 2.4% For Week As Yields, Foreign Selling Hit Sentiment
text:
'Bursa Sheds 2.4% For Week As Yields, Foreign Selling Hit Sentiment

'Bursa Malaysia ended the Sept 28-Oct 2 week sharply lower, with the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) losing 40.75 points, or 2.4%, to 1,630.87 from the previous Friday’s 1,671.62, as rising global bond yields, elevated oil prices and persistent foreign selling weighed on sentiment.  The benchmark started the week marginally lower, slipping 0.09% to 1,670.02 on Sept 28, as investors remained cautious amid a lack of fresh catalysts and continued external headwinds.  Selling intensified the next day, when the FBM KLCI tumbled 26.06 points, or 1.56%, to 1,643.96, pressured by surging bond yields and Brent crude prices around US$107 a barrel, which reignited inflation concerns and dampened risk appetite.  The market rebounded 0.43% to 1,651.17 on Sept 30 as bargain hunters returned following the sharp sell-off, although broader sentiment remained cautious ahead of key US inflation data.  That recovery proved short-lived, with the index plunging another 1.26% to 1,630.36 the following day, dragged by selling in heavyweights including Maybank, Public Bank, CIMB, TNB and IHH Healthcare. Weak domestic manufacturing activity and continued foreign outflows added to the pressure.  Bursa eked out a 0.03% gain to 1,630.87 to close out the trading week as bargain hunting cushioned the recent sell-off, but the rebound remained muted amid weakness across regional markets and caution ahead of US labour data.  Overall, the FBM KLCI recorded losses in three of the five sessions, with external rate and inflation concerns dominating trading despite intermittent bargain hunting.

title: 'Which Taxes Could Be Introduced Or Delayed In Budget 2027?
text:
'Which Taxes Could Be Introduced Or Delayed In Budget 2027?

'There is a growing sentiment that there will unlikely be any sweeping new taxes in Budget 2027, however stronger enforcement, wider e-invoicing adoption and refinements to existing taxes will offer more immediate opportunities to raise government revenue, according to tax expert Dr Veerinderjeet Singh.  The KPMG senior adviser on tax policy said the government is likely to remain conscious of cost-of-living pressures and its social agenda, limiting the appetite for substantial tax increases when Budget 2027 is tabled in Parliament on Oct 9. The government has similarly identified protecting households from rising living costs as one of the budget’s central priorities.  The report carried out by CIMB Securities highlighted that his central argument was that Malaysia should first “sweat our assets” — collecting more effectively from existing taxes and taxpayers — before turning to major new revenue instruments.  This would require greater investment in the Inland Revenue Board and Customs, particularly in data analytics to identify businesses outside the tax net and under-reporting among existing taxpayers.  GST Return Unlikely  Veerinderjeet does not expect the Goods and Services Tax (GST) to return in Budget 2027.  He estimated that the current Sales and Service Tax (SST) regime already covers about 78% to 80% of goods and services, approaching the breadth previously covered by GST.  Instead, he sees greater scope to improve the efficiency of SST, including considering broader exemptions for business inputs to reduce tax cascading along supply chains.  Such relief would, however, involve a trade-off because it would also reduce some government revenue.  E-invoicing is expected to become increasingly important in improving compliance and identifying previously unreported taxable activity. Malaysia’s rollout has already been implemented progressively across businesses according to annual turnover, with the framework most recently updated in August.  Veerinderjeet said wider participation could help bring more businesses into the tax system, although policymakers must recognise the technology and compliance costs faced by smaller companies.  No Dividend Tax Hike, CGT Expansion Expected  Budget 2027 is also unlikely to raise the existing 2% tax on annual dividend income exceeding RM100,000, although Veerinderjeet believes the rate could potentially increase over the longer term.  Similarly, he does not expect capital gains tax to be extended to listed shares in the near term. Malaysia currently imposes CGT on specified disposals of unlisted shares by companies, with the regime having taken effect from March 2024.  A further increase in Malaysia’s 30% top personal income tax rate also appears unlikely given regional competitiveness considerations.

title: 'TNB Could Absorb Up to RM150 Million in Extra Costs From Expanded Electricity Relief, CIMB Securities Says
text:
'TNB Could Absorb Up to RM150 Million in Extra Costs From Expanded Electricity Relief, CIMB Securities Says

'TNB Could Absorb Up to RM150 Million in Extra Costs From Expanded Electricity Relief, CIMB Securities Says KUALA LUMPUR — Tenaga Nasional Bhd could absorb an additional RM120 million to RM150 million in costs between September and December 2026 following the expansion of government exemptions covering electricity-related charges for residential consumers, according to CIMB Securities. The brokerage said nearly one million additional households are expected to benefit after the monthly electricity consumption threshold for the exemptions was raised to 800 kilowatt-hours (kWh) from 600 kWh. The change brings the total number of residential consumers covered to more than eight million. The exemptions involve the Automatic Fuel Adjustment (AFA), retail charges and sales and service tax, reducing the immediate impact of electricity costs on a wider group of households. However, CIMB Securities said the arrangement means TNB is expected to absorb additional costs during the September-to-December protection period. The eventual financial impact will depend on the level of AFA charges during that period, which in turn is influenced by fuel costs. Unexpected cost for utility CIMB Securities described the development as a negative surprise because it had previously expected TNB to recover any government-sanctioned AFA subsidies through the Kumpulan Wang Industri Elektrik fund. The latest arrangement instead places an estimated RM120 million to RM150 million of additional costs on the national utility during the final four months of 2026. The research house noted that TNB had previously made a voluntary RM150 million corporate contribution towards the government’s tiered electricity rebate initiative between April and September 2020. That programme was introduced during the Covid-19 pandemic. CIMB Securities said it regarded the 2020 contribution differently because it was made in response to what it described as a severe and unprecedented crisis. The latest cost absorption therefore raises a broader question for investors over whether TNB could be required to shoulder similar costs beyond 2026. 2026 profit forecast trimmed Despite the additional burden, CIMB Securities maintained its “buy” recommendation on TNB and kept its discounted cash flow-based target price unchanged at RM15.90. The brokerage reduced its core net profit forecast for TNB’s full 2026 financial year by two per cent to account for the additional costs. Its core net profit forecasts for the 2027 and 2028 financial years were left largely unchanged. CIMB Securities said the immediate effect on TNB’s core earnings remained relatively small and was insufficient to change its valuation. Its longer-term concern centres instead on what could happen if fuel prices remain elevated and the expanded AFA exemptions continue beyond the end of 2026.

title: 'Bursa Malaysia opens higher on positive Wall Street momentum
text:
'Bursa Malaysia opens higher on positive Wall Street momentum

'KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia opened higher on Tuesday, in sync with Wall Street's positive overnight momentum, as muted oil prices following a recovery in West Asia crude exports offset a continued sell-off in US Treasuries. At 9.21am, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose 7.14 points, or 0.44 per cent, to 1,638.89 from Monday's close of 1,631.75. The index opened 4.63 points higher at 1,636.38. On the broader market, gainers outpaced losers 272 to 202, with 364 counters unchanged, 1,944 untraded and 13 suspended. Turnover stood at 440.19 million shares worth RM164.76 million. Malacca Securities Sdn Bhd said Wall Street's positive overnight performance saw the Dow Jones Industrial Average, S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite advance by 0.2 per cent, 0.7 per cent and 1.1 per cent, respectively, while the Brent crude oil and 10-year Treasury yield reached US$100.3 per barrel and 5.3 per cent, respectively. "Locally, we expect investors to remain selective ahead of the Budget 2027 announcement, with attention centred on potential beneficiary sectors. title: 'Are Chinese Malaysian-owned SMEs being ‘killed’ by the China onslaught?
text:
'Are Chinese Malaysian-owned SMEs being ‘killed’ by the China onslaught?

'The Gut Shot Podcast is joined by its geopolitical and economic consultant to governments and companies, Jason Leong. Signals from the ground have now raised alarm among segments of the Chinese Malaysian community. Malaysia’s private sector economy is largely driven by local ethnic Chinese businesses. Unlike the ecosystem of government-linked firms and investment companies, the private sector economy has none of the protection that bumiputra monopolies and oligopolies enjoy. The retail, mechanic workshops, construction services and supply chains, food and beverage and other service businesses are not abstract figures on an economist’s spreadsheet. They are livelihoods that have survived for decades. They have employed workers, paid taxes, supported families and funded the education of the next generation. Now a wave of imported competition from China, at scaled-down and even cut-throat prices, has reached our shores with devastating effect. When businesses across very different sectors begin telling the same story at the same time (vanishing margins, slowing customers, rising costs, price competition that cannot be met and a daily struggle to survive), we should not dismiss it as a series of isolated failures or a lack of competitiveness. This podcast explores the damage to local ethnic Chinese-driven small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in both macro and micro terms, calmly and without sentiment and makes some policy recommendations. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member It examines why, however efficient our supply chains become, resistance on scale alone will be futile: massive state subsidies, fierce internal competition within China that no other country can replicate, and a capital structure built to chase market share at any cost. The official macro numbers may not have captured this yet. Perhaps no one has measured it properly or raised the alarm. But the signals are real. By the time everyone agrees there is a crisis, many of these businesses could already be gone. If we fail to recognise the systemic forces behind China’s global dominance and act accordingly, we may be witnessing the beginning of the end of the traditional, generations-old Chinese Malaysian SMEs ecosystem. title: 'Maybank Enters Into An Unconditional Agreement To Acquire Ageas Stake In MAHB After BNM Nod
text:
'Maybank Enters Into An Unconditional Agreement To Acquire Ageas Stake In MAHB After BNM Nod

'Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) has entered into an unconditional agreement to acquire Ageas Insurance International NV’s remaining 30.95% stake in Maybank Ageas Holdings Bhd (MAHB) for RM4.83 billion cash, paving the way for the banking group to take full ownership of its insurance and takaful business.  Maybank said it signed the share purchase agreement on Sept 8, 2026 with Ageas and its ultimate holding company, Ageas SA/NV, following approvals received from Bank Negara Malaysia on Sept 1.  The transaction involves 78.00 million MAHB shares, which will be acquired through Maybank’s wholly-owned subsidiary Etiqa International Holdings Sdn Bhd (EIHSB).  Upon completion, Maybank will effectively own 100% of MAHB, giving the banking group greater control over the future expansion of its Etiqa insurance and takaful franchise.  The deal follows an implementation agreement signed between Maybank and Ageas on Aug 3, which was conditional on receiving the necessary regulatory approvals.  The RM4.83 billion purchase consideration will be settled entirely in cash on completion.  As part of the transaction, MAHB will also distribute a RM799.99 million dividend to its existing shareholders on the completion date.  Of this, EIHSB will receive RM552.38 million, while Ageas will receive RM247.61 million.  EIHSB will additionally pay Ageas a RM34.17 million ticking fee, accrued from Aug 1 to Sept 11, the targeted completion date for the acquisition.  Maybank said full ownership of MAHB would allow it to strengthen the insurance and takaful business by deepening penetration among its existing and new banking customers.

title: 'PTT Synergy beli 4 kilang dalam pembinaan bernilai RM32 juta di Klang sebelum disewakan

'PTT Synergy beli 4 kilang dalam pembinaan bernilai RM32 juta di Klang sebelum disewakan

'KUALA LUMPUR 5 Okt — PTT Synergy Group Berhad bakal memperluas portfolio hartanah dengan pemerolehan empat unit kilang bernilai hampir RM32 juta di Klang, Selangor, yang disasarkan menjana pendapatan sewa berulang daripada penyewa industri. Menerusi makluman tambahan kepada Bursa Malaysia, ia berkata anak syarikat tidak langsung milik penuhnya, PTT Assets Sdn Bhd, akan memperoleh empat bidang tanah bersama unit kilang yang sedang atau akan dibina dengan jumlah pertimbangan tunai RM31.997 juta. Menurut kumpulan tersebut, pemerolehan itu bertujuan mengembangkan portfolio pelaburan hartanah kumpulan dan mewujudkan aliran pendapatan sewa berulang menerusi penyewaan keempat-empat unit kilang kepada penyewa industri. "PTT merancang memulakan proses mencari penyewa serta rundingan pajakan sepanjang tempoh pembinaan, dengan operasi sewaan disasarkan bermula selepas projek siap dan milikan kosong diserahkan, tertakluk kepada kerja pengubahsuaian yang diperlukan," katanya. Keempat-empat hartanah dijangka disiapkan dalam tempoh 36 bulan daripada tarikh perjanjian jual beli (SPA) masing-masing, dengan kerja pembinaan telah bermula pada 7 Januari 2026 dan kini mencapai sehingga peringkat rangka struktur bangunan, atau kira-kira 55% siap. Dari segi pembiayaan, risiko pembelian itu disokong kelulusan pinjaman daripada CIMB Bank Berhad dengan margin pembiayaan 90%, selain rebat Bumiputera 10% yang diberikan penjual. Berdasarkan terma pembayaran, 10% daripada harga pembelian perlu dibayar sebaik sahaja setiap SPA ditandatangani, manakala baki bayaran dibuat secara berperingkat mengikut kemajuan pembinaan sehingga notis milikan kosong dikeluarkan. "Pembelian itu turut mengambil kira transaksi hartanah perindustrian berdekatan, termasuk sebuah kilang berkembar di Bukit Raja Prime Industrial Park seluas 1,854.99 meter persegi yang didagangkan pada RM8.5 juta pada Jun 2026," jelas PTT. Satu lagi perbandingan ialah kilang berkembar di Bukit Raja 3 Industrial Park berkeluasan 2,024.99 meter persegi yang direkodkan pada harga RM7.689 juta pada Mac 2026. Sekiranya penjual gagal menyerahkan milikan kosong dalam tempoh 36 bulan daripada tarikh SPA, penjual perlu membayar ganti rugi dipersetujui pada kadar 5% setahun berdasarkan jumlah bayaran yang telah dibuat PTT sehingga tarikh penyerahan sebenar. Dari segi kedudukan kewangan, nisbah penggearan proforma PTT dijangka meningkat kepada 2.01 kali selepas pemerolehan berbanding 1.91 kali setakat 30 Jun 2025, berdasarkan kedudukan kewangan proforma yang dinyatakan syarikat. - DagangNews.com

'Share price soars as earnings continue to shine

'This article first appeared in The Edge Malaysia Weekly on October 5, 2026 - October 11, 2026 AMMB Holdings Bhd Once again, AMMB Holdings Bhd (KL:AMBANK) is taking home The Edge Billion Ringgit Club (BRC) award for Highest returns to shareholders over three years under the financial services category. Notably, its share price has climbed steadily over the last five years, with the most significant jump recorded between 2024 and 2025. The stock gained 41.9% from RM3.70 on March 31, 2024 to RM5.25 on March 28, 2025. Between March 28, 2025 and March 31, 2026, the banking group’s share price continued its upward trajectory, reaching RM6.59, before hitting another record high of RM7.37 on Aug 12. Much of the enthusiasm about the stock can be linked to the potential return of excess capital to shareholders, which could either come in the form of higher dividends or through other capital return initiatives. AMMB, under its five-year strategic plan called “Winning Together 2029” (WT29), aims to double its dividend per share by the financial year ending March 31, 2029 (FY2029) from 22.6 sen in FY2024. This would be supported by earnings growth and capital optimisation, with Basel 3.1 reforms providing a meaningful upside catalyst. AMMB has already been increasing its dividend payout ratio, from 40% to 50% in FY2025, exceeding its earlier dividend payout ratio guidance of 35% to 40%. Total dividends increased from 22.6 sen in FY2024 to 30.2 sen in FY2025 and 35 sen in FY2026. Its three-year compound annual growth rate for shareholder returns totalled 27.9% for the period between March 31, 2023 and March 31, 2026. The increase in dividends can also be attributed to the yearly improvements in earnings. In FY2026, the group achieved its highest-ever net profit of RM2.1 billion, 5% higher than the previous year’s RM2 billion, driven by both net interest income and non-interest income. Net profit was RM1.87 billion in FY2024. Net interest income rose 4.5% in FY2026, backed by higher margins, while non-interest income grew 5.1% mainly from trading gains. For FY2026, the bank recorded a return on equity (ROE) of 10%, in line with its guidance to analysts. The group’s ROE has stayed at 10% over the last three financial years. In the recent 1QFY2027 financial performance, AMMB’s net profit came in at RM520.23 million, up slightly from RM516.18 million in the previous year on account of improvement in net interest income growth. The earnings were within analyst expectations. Non-interest income grew 5.1% year on year, supported by stronger wealth management fee income but net interest income was softer, compressing to 1.93% in 1QFY2027 from 1.97% in 4QFY2026, as competitive asset pricing and funding mix pressures weighed on margins. CIMB Securities has downgraded its call on AMMB to “hold” with an unchanged target price of RM7.35, based on 1.09 times price-to-book value (PBV).

title: 'Import Duty On Minted Gold Bars Drops To 0% From 1 November 2026
text:
'Import Duty On Minted Gold Bars Drops To 0% From 1 November 2026

'Small gold bars of 1g, 5g, or 10g have become a common way for people to put money aside a little at a time. Since 8 June 2026, though, anyone buying imported minted bars may have been paying for a 10% import duty included in the price. The Customs Duties (Amendment) Order 2026, P.U. (A) 350, cuts that duty from 10% to 0% from 1 November 2026. Gold Bars Covered By The Cut The cut applies to minted (stamped) gold bars, the small bars people buy to save. The most common sizes are 1g to 50g. The duty only ever applied to imported bars, so bars minted in Malaysia were never taxed and their prices have no duty to lose. Bank Muamalat sells imported bars, and it told customers in May that these bars would cost more once the duty applied. According to Tomei Consolidated group managing director Datuk Ng Yih Pyng, large cast bars, which weigh 1kg and up and are used by manufacturers, are classed differently and were already duty-free. Jewellery isn’t affected either. So this matters to you if you buy imported minted bars, or if you convert gold in your account into an imported physical bar. Possible Savings On An Imported Bar The duty is 10% of what a bar is worth when it arrives in Malaysia. So a bar worth RM100 costs the seller RM110 once the duty is added. When the duty is removed, RM110 drops back to RM100. That’s a saving of RM10 out of RM110, or about 9.1% off what the seller paid for the bar. On 5 October, Bank Muamalat sold a gold bar at RM605.02 a gram and gold in its account at RM584.53 a gram, according to its own price board. If the account price has no duty in it, the RM20.49 difference is the most the duty could be adding to each gram of the bar. The table below shows what that means for each bar size Bank Muamalat sells. RinggitPlus worked out these amounts using Bank Muamalat’s bar and account prices on 5 October 2026. Prices will change with the gold price. The real saving will be less than this, because part of the difference pays for making and packaging the bar, and that cost stays. Buying Now Or Waiting Until November If you buy gold every month through a gold account or gold savings plan, you probably don’t need to change anything. The Malaysia Gold Association’s president, Datuk Seri Louis Ng, said in September that the duty applies to minted bars in finished, packaged form, and not to kilobars and cast bars. So gold held in an account may not be affected, but check with your bank. If you’re planning to buy an imported minted bar in October, ask the seller two things. Did they pay the import duty on this bar, and will the price change after 1 November? Then work out how much more the bar costs than the seller’s gold account price, per gram. Do this now, and then again in the first week of November. If that difference shrinks, the duty removal has made the bar cheaper. If it doesn’t, any price drop is just the gold price moving.

title: 'Maybank Falls Below RM10 for First Time in Nine Months as Rising Bond Yields Hurt Banking Stocks
text:
'Maybank Falls Below RM10 for First Time in Nine Months as Rising Bond Yields Hurt Banking Stocks

'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): Malayan Banking Bhd (KL:MAYBANK) fell below RM10 for the first time in nearly nine months and banking stocks mostly declined on Thursday amid rising bond yields. Higher yields generally hurt banks as they take larger paper losses from lower prices of the bonds they hold, which eats into capital and forces them to book losses if they sell. Investors may also demand higher returns on corporate bonds, affecting appetite for new issuances. That would weigh on banks’ near term non-interest income as well as their capital ratios, Affin Hwang Investment Bank flagged in a note on Thursday. Maybank, the country’s top bank in terms of assets, fell for the third straight day and closed down 0.4% at RM9.95. CIMB Group Holdings Bhd (KL:CIMB) and Hong Leong Bank Bhd (KL:HLBANK) each declined over 1%. The Bursa Malaysia Financial Services Index, which also tracks non-bank firms such as insurers and stockbrokers, fell to its lowest level in 10 months. The US Federal Reserve raised interest rates earlier this month for the first time in three years, sending the yield on the 10-year benchmark Malaysian Government Securities to as high as 4.18% before moderating. A growing number of economists expect Bank Negara Malaysia to raise the overnight policy rate in November during the final scheduled monetary policy review for the year. Rising yields tend to lead to higher corporate bond yields, which also tie-in to capital raising decisions both for banks and other corporates and, subsequently, fee income to the banks, Affin Hwang said. Maybank and Alliance Bank Malaysia Bhd (KL:ABMB) have on their books the longest bond duration — the length of time for a bond to repay its cost in cash flows while also being a measure of sensitivity to changes in interest rates — according to the research house’s analysis. Public Bank Bhd (KL:PBBANK) and Hong Leong Bank, meanwhile, have the shortest duration. 'Mustapha Proposes Committee to Work Out Mechanism for Sabah, Sarawak Parliamentary Seat Increase

'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 5): Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Sabah and Sarawak) Datuk Mustapha Sakmud has proposed the establishment of a special committee under the Technical Committee of the Malaysia Agreement 1963 Implementation Action Council (MTPMA63) to work out the mechanism for increasing parliamentary seats for Sabah and Sarawak. He also proposed that the special committee be co-chaired by him and Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said. “The increase in the number of members of Parliament from Sabah and Sarawak has been included in the agenda of MTPMA63 and its Technical Committee meetings, and has also been discussed extensively at Cabinet meetings. “Following the decision, I held preliminary discussions with the Election Commission (EC) to seek its views and determine the next course of action,” he said during the question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat on Monday. He said this in response to a supplementary question from Datuk Willie Mongin (GPS-Puncak Borneo), who sought clarification on the mechanisms and legislative steps required to increase parliamentary seats for the two states. Mustapha said discussions on the matter would continue at upcoming meetings of the MTPMA63 Technical Committee. Meanwhile, he said 13 of the 26 matters under the MTPMA63 negotiation platform had been categorised as resolved, following decisions made at the first MTPMA63 meeting held on Sept 11. “Of the 26 matters, three have been categorised as partially resolved, five remain unresolved, while another five have been brought before the prime minister, the Sarawak premier and the Sabah chief minister for discussion,” he said. Mustapha said the MA63-related matters brought before the highest level for discussion and decision-making included oil royalties and petroleum cash payments, stamp duties, the Territorial Sea Act 2012, and state rights over the continental shelf. He said the Madani government was committed to expediting the resolution of all claims under the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63), although the timeframe for resolving each claim was subject to the relevant legal processes. “The Madani government remains firmly committed to ensuring the prudent and inclusive implementation of MA63, grounded in the spirit of strong federalism,” he said. title: 'RHB Group maintains Malaysia's 2026 growth forecast at 5.4pct
text:
'RHB Group maintains Malaysia's 2026 growth forecast at 5.4pct

'KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's gross domestic product (GDP) for 2026 is projected at 5.4 per cent, underpinned by resilient domestic demand and sustained strength in electric and electronic (E&E) exports, according to RHB Group. In RHB's Global Economics Outlook for Q4 2026, group chief economist and head of market research, Barnabas Gan said the bank revised the headline inflation forecast to 1.9 per cent for 2026 from 2.1 per cent previously, reflecting softer-than-expected price pressures. For the first eight months of the year, inflation averaged 1.8 per cent, alongside the restoration of the BUDI95 monthly quota and an increase in the diesel subsidy quota from September. "For the rest of 2026, the inflation trajectory will be shaped by global commodity price movements, changes in domestic policies, as well as potential upside from food inflation," he said. Gan added that domestic policy measures, such as RON95 and diesel subsidy, stable food prices, stable demand conditions and a relatively stable ringgit, as well as gradual pass-through to consumer prices should help keep inflation contained. Meanwhile, he said the overnight policy rate is expected to remain unchanged at 2.75 per cent at the upcoming November Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting amid manageable inflation. Moving forward, Gan said RHB Bank expects Bank Negara Malaysia to deliver a token 25 basis points (bps) hike in the first half of 2027 (1H 2027) as a normalisation move towards a more neutral policy setting rather than a response to significant inflationary pressures. He also expects the 2026 fiscal deficit to remain broadly on track towards the government's 3.5 per cent of GDP target, although risks are tilted towards a modest overshoot given the relatively high deficit in the first half of 2026 (1H 2026) and uncertainties surrounding fuel subsidy expenditure. At the same time, the bank is maintaining its current account surplus forecast at 2.4 per cent of GDP for 2026, versus a 2.5 per cent surplus in 1H 2026. "The goods surplus should remain supported by resilient E&E exports amid the global technology cycle, while robust tourism receipts and information and communication technology services exports should underpin the services account. "Together, these should sustain Malaysia's current account surplus," added Gan.

title: 'AG cautions on use of AI, effective human oversight is still essential
text:
'AG cautions on use of AI, effective human oversight is still essential

'AG cautions on use of AI, effective human oversight is still essential KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): While the emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) has been used extensively and relied upon in the last few years, Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar cautioned for the need for human oversight in its usage. Dusuki said there is no doubt that AI offers significant opportunities in various sectors. For instance, he said, in healthcare, it can assist clinical judgement while in the corporate sphere, it can support decision-making, improve efficiency, and help professionals process increasingly complex information. “But as our reliance on these systems grows, so, too, does the importance of understanding how they are used and how they are governed. We need to ask some very practical questions: How reliable is the information produced by an AI system? What are the limits of its capabilities? Who is responsible for checking its output?” he said. He questioned what would happen when the AI system does not perform as expected. “These are not merely questions about technology. They are questions of governance, professional responsibility, and human oversight. Increasingly, they may also have consequences for legal liability and insurance. “For any institution adopting AI, it is therefore important to understand why the technology is being used, what risks may arise from its use, and what safeguards are necessary. Technology may assist professional judgement, but effective human oversight remains essential,” he reminded. Dusuki was delivering his keynote address at the Inaugural Financial Lines Forum at a hotel here. Also present were Lembaga Tabung Haji chairman and RHB Bank founder Tan Sri Abdul Rashid Hussin, who delivered a special address, and former Federal Court judge Tan Sri Zainun Ali, former Chief Judge of Malaya Tan Sri Hasnah Mohamed Hashim, as well as former and current judges. The AG said that while there are continuing issues in the usage of AI, there is a need to use it responsibly. Dusuki said the use of AI requires engagement among those who develop the technology, those who deploy it, those who rely on it, and those who assess and manage the risks associated with its use. Hence, he welcomed the organisation of such a forum like the Financial Lines Forum as it brings together legal professionals, healthcare practitioners, corporate leaders, insurers, brokers, and other stakeholders. “We have an opportunity to learn from one another, to better understand the risks and opportunities before us, and to consider how our respective professions can respond responsibly to a rapidly changing environment. “Ultimately, the question is not simply what artificial intelligence can do. The more important question is, how we, as professionals, choose to use it responsibly,” he added.

'KUALA LUMPUR 5 Okt — PTT Synergy Group Berhad bakal memperluas portfolio hartanah dengan pemerolehan empat unit kilang bernilai hampir RM32 juta di Klang, Selangor, yang disasarkan menjana pendapatan sewa berulang daripada penyewa industri. Menurut kumpulan tersebut, pemerolehan itu bertujuan mengembangkan portfolio pelaburan hartanah kumpulan dan mewujudkan aliran pendapatan sewa berulang menerusi penyewaan keempat-empat unit kilang kepada penyewa industri. "PTT merancang memulakan proses mencari penyewa serta rundingan pajakan sepanjang tempoh pembinaan, dengan operasi sewaan disasarkan bermula selepas projek siap dan milikan kosong diserahkan, tertakluk kepada kerja pengubahsuaian yang diperlukan," katanya. Keempat-empat hartanah dijangka disiapkan dalam tempoh 36 bulan daripada tarikh perjanjian jual beli (SPA) masing-masing, dengan kerja pembinaan telah bermula pada 7 Januari 2026 dan kini mencapai sehingga peringkat rangka struktur bangunan, atau kira-kira 55% siap. Dari segi pembiayaan, risiko pembelian itu disokong kelulusan pinjaman daripada CIMB Bank Berhad dengan margin pembiayaan 90%, selain rebat Bumiputera 10% yang diberikan penjual. Berdasarkan terma pembayaran, 10% daripada harga pembelian perlu dibayar sebaik sahaja setiap SPA ditandatangani, manakala baki bayaran dibuat secara berperingkat mengikut kemajuan pembinaan sehingga notis milikan kosong dikeluarkan. title: 'A trader’s guide to navigating Budget 2027
text:
'A trader’s guide to navigating Budget 2027

'KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia’s consumer and construction stocks may emerge as beneficiaries of next year’s spending plan as Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim seeks to ease living costs while maintaining fiscal prudence. Anwar, who also serves as finance minister, is expected to announce measures to support households and sustain infrastructure spending when he unveils the annual budget on Friday. Investors will also be on watch for any update on a potential minimum-wage revision, which may boost consumption but add to earnings risk for companies. While Malaysia’s economy remains resilient, a renewed climb in oil prices is driving up fuel-subsidy costs, potentially weighing on the fiscal outlook and investor confidence. The spending plan ahead of a national election due early 2028 comes as Anwar seeks to rebuild public support following recent state poll setbacks. “Given the proximity to the 16th general election or GE16, this will be a people’s budget,” said Alexander Chia, analyst at RHB Research. “Social protection initiatives targeted at the lower and mid-income groups will be positive for the consumer, property, transport and healthcare sectors.” The country’s stock benchmark has fallen nearly 3% this year, lagging some South-East Asian peers including Thailand and Vietnam, as fiscal and political risks weigh. Moreover, foreign funds have sold US$1.59bil of local shares on a net basis so far in 2026. Several key areas warrant close attention in the Budget 2027 announcement. Budget 2027 is poised to include targeted assistance and measures to boost wages as the government seeks to temper the prospect of rising inflation on the cost of living. A likely increase in cash handouts to around RM17bil from RM15bil in 2026 should support mass-market consumption, according to Apex Securities analyst Wong Kai Heng. That should benefit retailers such as 99 Speed Mart Retail Holdings Bhd and Padini Holdings Bhd, as well as food and beverage companies including Nestle (Malaysia) Bhd, CCK Consolidated Holdings Bhd and Oriental Kopi Holdings Bhd. Analysts expect a modest increase in the development expenditure, which would provide continued support for infrastructure investment. Key projects that could feature under Budget 2027 include the light rail transit in Penang, the Northern Perak Water Supply Scheme and basic infrastructure projects in Sabah and Sarawak. “Potential beneficiaries of development expenditure expansion would be concentrated among contractors and suppliers exposed to water infrastructure and pipe replacement, flood mitigation, rural infrastructure, grid investment, and projects in Sabah and Sarawak,” Ivy Ng Lee Fang, an analyst at CIMB Securities, wrote in a report. That may boost firms in the construction industry, including Gamuda Bhd, IJM Corp Bhd and Malayan Cement Bhd.

title: 'ViTrox Hits New Record High as AI-driven Growth Boosts Outlook
text:
'ViTrox Hits New Record High as AI-driven Growth Boosts Outlook

'KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 22): Shares in ViTrox Corporation Bhd (KL:VITROX) hit their highest level since the company’s listing on the ACE Market in 2005 on Tuesday, driven by its strong growth prospects amid the AI infrastructure boom. ViTrox designs & manufactures vision inspection system & handler for back-end semiconductor industry. In a The Edge Malaysia weekly’s Sept 21-Sept 27 issue, its co-founder and managing director Datuk Chu Jenn Weng said the company’s numbers will double this year, with strong growth momentum expected to continue over the next few years. The Penang-based automated test equipment maker’s shares charted an all-time high of RM10.08 before closing up 21 sen or 2.2% at RM10 on Tuesday, giving the company a market capitalisation of a little under RM19 billion. The share price remains below the consensus 12-month target price of RM10.67, while the highest 12-month target price is RM13. The majority of analysts covering the company have a “buy” call on the stock, with 11 “buy” calls, two “hold” calls and one “sell” call. Analysts noted that ViTrox has positioned itself as a key beneficiary of AI infrastructure spending. Research houses have also upgraded their earnings forecasts, with Apex Securities raising its net profit forecasts for FY2026, FY2027 and FY2028 to RM275.6 million, RM362.4 million and RM408.2 million, respectively, citing sustained AI infrastructure demand. CIMB Securities noted that ViTrox’s 1HFY2026 results exceeded expectations, coming in at more than 60% of its full-year consensus estimate. The research house reiterated its “buy” rating with a target price of RM10.00 and raised its FY2026–FY2028 earnings per share estimates by 28% to 37%, citing expanding order books, a favourable product mix and recurring service income. ViTrox saw its revenue double year-on-year in the second quarter ended June 30 (2QFY2026) to RM375 million from RM183 million in the same period last year. Net profit for the quarter jumped to RM85.04 million, bringing the company’s cumulative net profit for the first half of 2026 to RM136.24 million, surpassing its full-year net profit of RM133.18 million in 2025. Chu said the optimism surrounding the company is understandable, given that, much like its peers in the semiconductor-related industry, ViTrox is operating at full capacity and expanding to cope with the surge in demand. title: 'MKH bakal dinyahsenarai selepas Batu Kawan kuasai 95.16% saham | DagangNews - Berita Bisnes Anda
text:
'MKH bakal dinyahsenarai selepas Batu Kawan kuasai 95.16% saham | DagangNews - Berita Bisnes Anda

'KUALA LUMPUR 1 Okt – MKH Bhd bakal dinyahsenarai daripada Bursa Malaysia selepas Batu Kawan Bhd bersama anak syarikatnya, Whitmore Holdings Sdn Bhd serta pihak yang bertindak bersama mereka menguasai 95.16% saham syarikat pemaju hartanah itu. Jumlah pegangan tersebut bersamaan 548.85 juta saham MKH setakat penutupan dagangan pada 30 Sept 2026, menurut kenyataan yang dikeluarkan oleh Maybank Investment Bank Bhd bagi pihak Batu Kawan dan Whitmore. Dengan pegangan yang sudah melepasi 90%, Batu Kawan dan Whitmore kini boleh mengambil alih baki saham MKH yang masih dipegang pemegang saham yang tidak menerima tawaran pengambilalihan tersebut. Baki saham MKH akan diambil alih secara wajib Langkah itu akan dibuat di bawah Seksyen 222(1) Akta Pasaran Modal dan Perkhidmatan 2007 yang membolehkan baki saham diperoleh secara wajib. Tawaran pengambilalihan pada harga RM2 sesaham itu masih dibuka sehingga 8 Oktober 2026 selepas tarikh tutup asal pada 17 September lalu dilanjutkan. Selepas tempoh tawaran tamat, Bursa Malaysia Securities akan menggantung dagangan saham MKH selepas lima hari pasaran, sebelum Batu Kawan dan Whitmore meneruskan proses untuk menarik balik status penyenaraian MKH. Pengambilalihan MKH bernilai RM1.15 bilion Langkah Batu Kawan mengambil alih MKH bermula pada Mei lalu apabila Whitmore bersetuju membeli kepentingan 47.7% dalam MKH daripada anggota keluarga Chen pada harga RM2 sesaham, membabitkan nilai RM549.8 juta. Pembelian itu kemudiannya disusuli tawaran kepada pemegang saham MKH yang lain pada harga sama bagi membolehkan Batu Kawan meningkatkan pegangannya dalam syarikat tersebut. Secara keseluruhan, pengambilalihan MKH untuk menjadikannya syarikat persendirian bernilai sehingga RM1.15 bilion, termasuk kos pembelian kepentingan awal daripada keluarga Chen. Tawaran RM2 sesaham terima pandangan berbeza Bagaimanapun, tawaran tersebut sebelum ini mendapat pandangan berbeza daripada penasihat bebas MKH dan MKH Oil Palm (East Kalimantan) Bhd, iaitu cabang perladangan MKH yang disenaraikan secara berasingan. Kenanga Investment Bank Bhd, yang bertindak sebagai penasihat bebas MKH, menilai tawaran RM2 sesaham itu sebagai “tidak adil tetapi munasabah”, dengan mengambil kira harga tawaran yang lebih rendah daripada nilai aset wajar MKH. Bagi MKH Oil Palm pula, Mainstreet Advisers Sdn Bhd menggesa pemegang saham menolak tawaran 66.26 sen sesaham daripada Batu Kawan, yang disifatkannya sebagai “tidak adil dan tidak munasabah”. Menurut Mainstreet, harga tawaran itu mewakili diskaun 47% kepada nilai aset bersih (NAV) MKH Oil Palm. Pada masa sama, Batu Kawan bercadang mengekalkan MKH Oil Palm sebagai syarikat yang disenaraikan di Bursa Malaysia.- DagangNews.com

title: 'Trading Of MKH Shares To Be Suspended

MKH said Bursa Malaysia will suspend trading in its shares upon the expiry of five market days from the extended closing date of the offer. Following the acceptance level, Whitmore and Batu Kawan will invoke subsection 222(1) of the Capital Markets and Services Act 2007 to compulsorily acquire the remaining shares from dissenting shareholders. Following the suspension, Whitmore and Batu Kawan intend to procure MKH to take the necessary steps to withdraw its listing status from Bursa Malaysia’s Official List.  If the delisting is completed, MKH shares will no longer be traded on the Main Market.  The takeover offer will remain open for acceptance until 5pm on Oct 8, 2026.

title: 'MUFG Sees Ringgit Dipping Below RM4 Against US Dollar by 3Q 2027
text:
'MUFG Sees Ringgit Dipping Below RM4 Against US Dollar by 3Q 2027

'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 5): The ringgit is expected to outperform most Asian currencies in the final quarter of 2026, supported by Malaysia’s strong electronics exports despite pressure from higher oil prices, according to MUFG Bank. It also expects Bank Negara Malaysia to maintain the overnight policy rate at 2.75% until the third quarter of next year as inflation remains contained. The ringgit was trading around 4.09 against the US dollar on Monday morning. MUFG expects it to strengthen to 4.03 by end-2026, before advancing further to 3.98 by the third quarter of 2027. MUFG expects the ringgit to be the strongest performing Asian currency covered in its latest foreign-exchange outlook. “Malaysia’s electronics surplus continues to cushion the oil shock,” MUFG said, adding that Malaysia's trade position remains relatively resilient amid elevated energy prices. “This means higher oil prices are likely to remain a headwind for the ringgit rather than derail its medium-term outlook,” MUFG said. Malaysia is also benefiting from continued investment in information and communications technology, including data centres and cloud computing. Services investment approvals rose more than 20% year-on-year in the first half of 2026, supported largely by ICT-related investments. MUFG said stronger US spending on computers and related equipment has also helped support demand for Malaysian electrical and electronics exports. “MYR fundamentals remain intact despite higher oil prices and the recent bond sell-off,” the bank said. While near-term volatility could persist as investors watch higher fuel-subsidy costs and global bond yields, MUFG said Malaysia’s resilient external position, improving capital flows and attractive valuations should continue to support the ringgit over the medium term. The bank also pointed to Malaysia’s stronger economic growth, with gross domestic product expanding 6% year-on-year in the second quarter, compared with an average pre-pandemic growth pace of 4.9%. title: 'Maybank completes Maybank Ageas buyout
text:
'Maybank completes Maybank Ageas buyout

'KUALA LUMPUR: Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) has completed the acquisition of the remaining 30.95 per cent stake in Maybank Ageas Holdings Bhd. This gives the banking group full ownership of the holding company for its Etiqa insurance and takaful business in Malaysia and Singapore. The transaction follows Maybank's share purchase agreement with Ageas Insurance International NV on Sept 8 and regulatory approval from Bank Negara Malaysia received on Sept 1. With the completion, Maybank Ageas becomes a wholly owned subsidiary of Maybank. Maybank president and group chief executive officer Datuk Seri Khairussaleh Ramli said the acquisition marks a significant milestone as the group seeks to strengthen Etiqa's position as a national insurance and takaful champion, while expanding its footprint across Southeast Asia. He said the move also supports Maybank's ROAR30 strategy to build a stronger regional franchise and establish a global takaful powerhouse. "With Maybank Ageas being a wholly owned subsidiary of Maybank, it strengthens Etiqa's position as a national insurance and takaful champion, driving deeper penetration of Maybank's customer base," said Khairussaleh. Full ownership is expected to give Maybank greater flexibility to integrate its banking, wealth and protection offerings, particularly across its regional customer base. Khairussaleh said Maybank intends to unlock further value through cross-selling and more integrated, personalised financial solutions. The acquisition should also support more effective capital management within Maybank Ageas and at the wider Maybank group level, potentially improving the insurance business's efficiency and resilience. Etiqa will continue to operate as one of Maybank's key brands, offering life and general conventional insurance alongside family and general takaful products through multiple distribution channels. "The Etiqa brand remains a strong and well-established insurance and takaful franchise, and it will continue to be positioned as one of Maybank's flagship brands," said Khairussaleh. With Maybank's extensive customer base and distribution network behind it, Etiqa is expected to pursue growth opportunities as demand rises for more integrated and personalised protection solutions. Maybank also acknowledged Ageas' contribution to the development of the Etiqa franchise over the past 25 years.

title: 'Creador acquires RHB building in Jalan Tun H S Lee and Bangunan UOB in Medan Pasar
text:
'Creador acquires RHB building in Jalan Tun H S Lee and Bangunan UOB in Medan Pasar

'Creador acquires RHB building in Jalan Tun H S Lee and Bangunan UOB in Medan Pasar This article first appeared in The Edge Malaysia Weekly on August 31, 2026 - September 6, 2026 SOUTHEAST Asian private equity firm Creador, through its philanthropic arm Creador Foundation, is understood to have recently added at least two more properties in downtown Kuala Lumpur to its growing city-centre portfolio — the historic RHB building in Jalan Tun H S Lee and Bangunan UOB in Medan Pasar, according to sources familiar with the matter. The Edge reported in July that the RHB building, a 13-storey office block located at 75 Jalan Tun H S Lee, had been on the market with a reserve price of RM30 million. Sources familiar with the deal say the building has changed hands close to the reserve price. The property carries considerable heritage weight. It was originally the landmark headquarters of Kwong Yik Bank, Malaya’s first local bank, founded in 1913. The building was formally opened in 1965 by then prime minister Tunku Abdul Rahman Putra Al-Haj and became part of RHB’s lineage after Rashid Hussain Bhd took a 75% stake in Kwong Yik Bank in 1996, ahead of its merger with DCB Bank the following year to form RHB Bank. RHB has already announced that its branch at the address will cease operations in January 2027. Details on the Bangunan UOB deal at 10-12 Medan Pasar are limited, although the road itself sits in the same historic banking and commercial belt as Jalan Tun H S Lee, just north of Dataran Merdeka — squarely within the footprint of the areas Creador, together with its founders’ Alaka Holdings Trust, has been actively involved in restoration initiatives. According to sources, Creador Foundation bought Bangunan UOB and the two shoplots next to it for slightly less than RM40 million. During a visit to the area on a Friday afternoon, the transformation to the area was apparent with ongoing construction and restoration works. A source tells The Edge that of the 27 buildings in the Medan Pasar area, 17 of them are believed to have been acquired by Creador while the other 10 have been leased. On Aug 13, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh announced a collaboration between Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) and Creador Foundation to revitalise Medan Pasar’s public space as well as improve rainwater management. The acquisitions of the buildings would extend a heritage-property push that Creador, through its philanthropic arm Creador Foundation, has been on since 2024, when it began restoration work around Medan Pasar and Central Market in Kuala Lumpur’s historic district. Its efforts have already delivered several visible wins, with the revival of a shuttered row of shophouses in Medan Pasar, including the Sin Seng Nam corner lot, now home to the popular KLCG Confectionery & Bakery.

'Asteel lantik bekas Ketua Polis Negara Razarudin sebagai pengerusi selepas Clifford Hii ambil alih syarikat

'KUALA LUMPUR 7 Okt - Asteel Group Berhad melantik bekas Ketua Polis Negara Tan Sri Razarudin Husain @ Abd Rasid sebagai pengerusi bukan eksekutif bebas dan pemegang saham pengawal Datuk Clifford Hii Toh Leong sebagai timbalan pengerusi eksekutif, berkuat kuasa pada Selasa. Perubahan lembaga pengarah itu menyusuli penutupan tawaran pengambilalihan mandatori pada 5 Oktober yang menyaksikan syarikat pelaburan Clifford, Hii Capital Holdings Sdn Bhd, memegang 53.08% kepentingan dalam pengeluar keluli berkenaan. Clifford memperoleh kawalan pada Ogos menerusi pembelian 270 juta saham Asteel oleh Hii Capital, mewakili kepentingan 52.94%, dengan bayaran tunai RM20.25 juta atau 7.5 sen sesaham. Pembelian itu mencetuskan tawaran mandatori bagi baki saham pada harga yang sama. Jawatan Tan Sri (Dr) Soh Thian Lai ditukar daripada pengerusi eksekutif kepada pengarah eksekutif merangkap pengerusi emeritus, menurut makluman syarikat kepada Bursa Malaysia. Asteel turut melantik Esther Teh Oun Pheng dan Datuk Dr Lor Chee Leng sebagai pengarah bukan eksekutif bebas. Pengarah bukan eksekutif bukan bebas Christopher Hii Lu Ming serta pengarah bukan eksekutif bebas Yan Ying Chieh, Khor Hun Nee dan Wee Hiang Chyn meletakkan jawatan atas sebab peribadi. Pengalaman dalam keselamatan dan perkhidmatan kewangan Razarudin, 63, mempunyai pengalaman lebih empat dekad dalam keselamatan negara dan penguatkuasaan undang-undang. Ketua Polis Negara ke-14 itu bersara pada Jun 2025 dan turut berkhidmat sebagai pengerusi bukan eksekutif bebas Advancecon Holdings Berhad. Clifford, 43, mempunyai pengalaman lebih 20 tahun dalam sektor pendidikan, hartanah dan teknologi kewangan. Bekas pengarah bukan eksekutif bukan bebas HCK Capital Group Berhad itu mengasaskan Gambit Group Sdn Bhd dan pernah memegang jawatan pengurusan kanan serta menganggotai lembaga pengarah, dengan pengalaman meliputi strategi korporat, pembangunan perniagaan, urus niaga, pelaburan, tadbir urus dan pengurusan projek. Beliau ialah anak kepada bekas wartawan yang beralih menjadi ahli perniagaan, Tan Sri Clement Hii Chii Kok, pengasas dan pengerusi eksekutif pemaju hartanah HCK Capital serta pengarah urusan kumpulan dan pemegang saham utama kumpulan pendidikan swasta SEG International. Esther Teh, 47, mengetuai audit dalaman dan pengurusan risiko di Usaha Tegas Sdn Bhd serta merupakan pengarah bebas OMS Energy Technologies Inc yang disenaraikan di Nasdaq. Beliau mempunyai pengalaman lebih 20 tahun dalam audit, pengurusan risiko, perundingan, pelaksanaan perkhidmatan bersama, operasi dan kawalan kewangan. Jawatan terdahulunya termasuk ketua audit dalaman dan pematuhan kumpulan di Silverlake Axis Ltd, ketua pengurusan risiko dan jaminan bagi bahagian digital kumpulan di Petroliam Nasional Bhd serta pengurus kanan perundingan pengurusan di Accenture.

title: 'Oct 23 ruling on bid to restrain RHB from closing Maritime Network's accounts
text:
'Oct 23 ruling on bid to restrain RHB from closing Maritime Network's accounts

'Oct 23 ruling on bid to restrain RHB from closing Maritime Network's accounts KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 24): The High Court here on Thursday fixed Oct 23 to rule on a shipping company's bid to restrain RHB Bank Bhd (LK:RHBBANK) from closing two of its long-standing accounts, pending the disposal of its full suit. Judicial Commissioner Elesabet Paya Wan set the date after hearing submissions from P Taneswaran, acting for Maritime Network Sdn Bhd, and the bank's counsel, Gan Khong Aik. Taneswaran submitted that the bank had failed to establish any breach of terms or requirements by the plaintiff, Maritime Network, that would justify closing its accounts. He further argued that the bank owed Maritime Network both a fiduciary duty and a duty of care. Gan countered that no fiduciary relationship or duty of care arose between the bank and the shipping company, submitting that the relationship between a bank and its customer is that of debtor and creditor. In October last year, the High Court granted a temporary injunction restraining RHB from closing the two long-standing accounts, pending the hearing of the company's application for a full injunction. According to court documents, the company has held a multi-currency account and a current account with RHB since 2005. On Oct 6, 2025, it received a termination notice dated Oct 1, 2025, stating that the bank intended to close both accounts and terminate all related services within 14 days, citing breaches of its internal policies and guidelines. The company, however, claimed that RHB had failed to specify which policies or guidelines were allegedly breached. The plaintiff said an ongoing dispute over the accounts had earlier led to its pre-trial discovery application being dismissed by the High Court on July 2, 2025. The company subsequently appealed to the Court of Appeal, which in December last year allowed its appeal against the dismissal of the pre-trial discovery application. The appellate court then ordered RHB to produce its minimum due diligence guidelines governing foreign-exchange transactions to the company within 45 days. Maritime Network further alleged that the bank's vague allegations placed it in a position of uncertainty, depriving it of any opportunity to defend itself. This conduct, the company asserted, amounted to an abuse of power that prejudiced its rights. title: 'Mandat Pengurus Keselamatan Kebakaran Bomba bagi 9,451 Bangunan Tonjolkan Permintaan Pematuhan untuk Unique Fire
text:
'Mandat Pengurus Keselamatan Kebakaran Bomba bagi 9,451 Bangunan Tonjolkan Permintaan Pematuhan untuk Unique Fire

'Langkah Malaysia menjadikan pemilik bangunan bertanggungjawab secara langsung terhadap keselamatan kebakaran dijangka meluaskan pasaran pematuhan bagi pembekal perlindungan kebakaran, sekali gus meletakkan Unique Fire Holdings Berhad (“Unique Fire”) antara syarikat yang berpotensi mendapat manfaat. Mulai 1 April 2027, pemilik 9,451 bangunan yang ditetapkan di bawah Akta Perkhidmatan Bomba akan diwajibkan melantik Pengurus Keselamatan Kebakaran (FSM) dan Pegawai Keselamatan Kebakaran (FSO), serta menubuhkan Organisasi Keselamatan Kebakaran (OKK) di premis masing-masing. Ketua Pengarah Jabatan Bomba dan Penyelamat Malaysia (JBPM), Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad berkata, keperluan itu selaras dengan Seksyen 27A Akta Perkhidmatan Bomba (Pindaan) 2025. Menurut beliau, mana-mana bangunan yang diperiksa dalam tempoh satu hingga dua tahun akan datang dan diwajibkan memiliki Perakuan Bomba perlu melaksanakan struktur baharu tersebut. Beliau berkata demikian selepas melancarkan program FSM dan FSO di Menara Merdeka Maybank, Kuala Lumpur pada 6 Oktober 2026, di mana kumpulan pertama seramai 174 FSM dan 324 FSO menerima sijil masing-masing. Perubahan utama melibatkan kaedah pembaharuan Perakuan Bomba. Selepas ini, JBPM akan menilai laporan pemeriksaan tahunan yang disediakan oleh FSM bagi tujuan pembaharuan perakuan, tanpa perlu menjalankan pemeriksaan fizikal ke atas setiap bangunan setiap tahun. JBPM kini mempunyai 13 penyedia latihan berdaftar dan telah mengeluarkan tender bagi menambah bilangan penyedia latihan serta jurulatih. Tanggungjawab pematuhan beralih kepada pemilik bangunan Rangka kerja ini memindahkan tanggungjawab keselamatan kebakaran harian daripada pihak berkuasa kepada pemilik bangunan dan kakitangan dalaman mereka yang bertauliah. Di bawah program ini, FSM menjalani kursus lima hari merangkumi pemeriksaan bangunan, perancangan pemindahan, pelaporan dan penyelenggaraan, manakala FSO menjalani kursus teknikal selama tiga hari. Dengan FSM bertanggungjawab ke atas laporan tahunan yang menjadi asas pembaharuan Perakuan Bomba, pemilik bangunan dijangka memberi penekanan lebih besar untuk memastikan alat pemadam api, gelung hos, pili bomba, sistem pemercik, peranti pengesan dan penggera serta sistem pemadaman kebakaran sentiasa berfungsi dengan baik. Ini menunjukkan permintaan yang lebih stabil bagi penggantian, penyelenggaraan dan pengisian semula peralatan di seluruh 9,451 premis yang ditetapkan, termasuk bangunan berpenghuni tinggi dan berisiko tinggi. Unique Fire, yang ditubuhkan pada 1997 dan beribu pejabat di Shah Alam, Selangor, terlibat dalam pemasangan, pembuatan dan pengedaran sistem, peralatan dan aksesori perlindungan kebakaran aktif untuk persekitaran terbina.

title: 'Sebungkus nasi bahagi dua, duit poket hanya RM300
text:
'Sebungkus nasi bahagi dua, duit poket hanya RM300

'TUMPAT: “Setiap hari saya beli sebungkus nasi pada waktu tengah hari. Separuh saya simpan untuk makan malam sepanjang tiga minggu di Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM).” Demikian cerita Siti Noor Hidayatul Hidayah Sudin, 20, apabila ibu bapanya hanya mampu memberikan wang saku RM300 ketika menghantarnya ke USM di Pulau Pinang. Katanya, itu sahaja simpanan yang ada kerana telah membayar yuran pendaftaran sebanyak RM850 bagi mengikuti pengajian Sarjana Muda Pendidikan Khas. Katanya, yuran pengajian sebanyak RM1,232 belum dijelaskan meskipun sudah tiga minggu belajar di USM. “Jika ibu dapat pinjam dengan saudara-mara, dia akan kirim wang dalam masa terdekat untuk jelaskan yuran pengajian tersebut,” katanya menerusi panggilan video semasa kunjungan Ahli Majlis Presiden Gabungan Pelajar Melayu Semenanjung (GPMS), Che Muhammad Redzuan Jihad di rumahnya di Kampung Bunohan di sini. Siti Noor Hidayatul Hidayah berkata, dia rela mengikat perut kerana tidak mahu menyusahkan ibunya, Ramlah Abdul Rahman, 52, yang tidak dapat berjalan sejak empat tahun lalu selepas menjalani pembedahan kaki kiri akibat penyakit kencing manis. Katanya, demi membiayai pengajiannya, ibunya yang berkerusi roda gigih membuat kuih bersama bapanya, Sudin Matsan, 63. Bagi Ramlah, doanya sentiasa mengiringi Siti Noor Hidayatul Hidayah yang bercita-cita mahu menjadi seorang pendidik meskipun berdepan masalah kewangan. “Wang simpanan sudah habis digunakan untuk rawatan perubatan saya. “Walaupun menghadapi kekangan kewangan, saya tahu anak saya kuat semangat untuk menempuhnya,” katanya. Sementara itu, Che Muhammad Redzuan berkata, GPMS akan menyalurkan maklumat kepada Bahagian Hal Ehwal Pelajar (HEP) USM untuk membantu Siti Noor Hidayatul Hidayah termasuk wang saku, baki yuran dan sumbangan komputer riba. Sumbangan boleh disalurkan ke akaun CIMB 7657421192, Siti Noor Hidayatul Hidayah. – UTUSAN

title: 'Tengku Ampuan Pahang rasmi Kejohanan Golf Wanita, The Ladies 2026
text:
'Tengku Ampuan Pahang rasmi Kejohanan Golf Wanita, The Ladies 2026

'PETALING JAYA: Kejohanan golf wanita, The Ladies 2026 rasmi membuka tirai kelmarin menerusi acara Pro-Am Diraja yang dirasmikan oleh Tengku Ampuan Pahang, Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah Almarhum Sultan Iskandar Al-Haj di The Mines Resort and Golf Club. Kejohanan yang berlangsung selama tiga hari itu menyaksikan penyertaan seramai 50 pemain merangkumi kelompok profesional dan amatur termasuklah kemunculan semula juara bertahan, Liyana Durisic serta atlet Olimpik negara, Kelly Tan. Menurut The Mines Resort & Golf Club, matlamat utama kejohanan itu adalah untuk melahirkan lebih ramai pemain berwibawa tempatan selain bertindak sebagai batu loncatan penting sebelum saingan bertaraf antarabangsa menjelang kejohanan Maybank Championship tidak lama lagi. Katanya, penganjuran itu membawa mesej yang jelas kepada generasi muda bahawa kerjaya dalam bidang sukan golf profesional bukan mustahil untuk dicapai oleh wanita Malaysia. “Ia adalah satu jemputan kepada generasi baharu untuk melihat golf profesional bukan sekadar sesuatu yang dimainkan di tempat lain di dunia tetapi sebagai laluan kerjaya yang boleh diceburi oleh wanita Malaysia,” katanya dalam kenyataan. Dalam pada itu, saingan Pro-Am Diraja hari ini menyaksikan pasukan yang dibarisi Dianna Lee, Ang Bee Ee, Jojo Goh dan digandingkan bersama pemain profesional Kelly Tan dinobatkan sebagai juara keseluruhan. Tempat kedua diraih oleh pasukan Miran Shin, Raina Azene Ramli, Nur Azreen dan pemain profesional Tan Ying Ying manakala kedudukan ketiga disandang oleh Yang Amat Mulia Che Puan Besar Kedah, Che Puan Hajah Hamimah Haji Hamidun, Datuk Norfaizah Zainal, June Yap bersama pemain profesional, Zulaikah Nasser. Menurutnya lagi, selain memperkukuh pembangunan bakat tempatan, penganjuran edisi kali ini turut mendapat sokongan padu pelbagai syarikat korporat terkemuka seperti Prudential, 100PLUS, Power Root dan Delon. Jelasnya, pihak penganjur turut mempunyai perancangan jangka panjang untuk meningkatkan kualiti kejohanan itu dengan sasaran hadiah terkumpul mencecah kira-kira RM12.5 juta pada masa hadapan. “Objektifnya bukan sekadar meningkatkan wang kemenangan tetapi untuk mewujudkan acara yang mempunyai status kukuh bagi menarik perhatian antarabangsa, di samping memberikan pemain Malaysia platform yang lebih berkesan ke pentas global,” katanya. – UTUSAN
